documents.title: H&P - Admission, Sepsis Secondary to Urinary Source
lines: ADMISSION HISTORY AND PHYSICAL
Time of note: 04:10, HD1
Pt is an 88-year-old female brought in by EMS from home for confusion and fever.
HPI:
Arrival to ED 02:10. Daughter at bedside gives most of the history.
[GCS] Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
Per daughter, 2 days of decreased appetite, foul-smelling urine, and one episode of incontinence, unusual for pt.
This morning pt would not get out of bed, then stopped answering questions appropriately by evening.
No cough, no sputum, no chest pain reported by daughter. No vomiting. No diarrhea. No fall.
No recent hospitalization. No indwelling catheter. No recent antibiotics.
TRIAGE VITALS:
[WBC] Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
BP 78/42, HR 118, [respiratory rate] Respiratory rate 30; SpO2 88% on RA, placed on 6L NC with SpO2 93%.
PMH:
Hypertension
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diet controlled
Chronic diastolic heart failure, compensated
Osteoarthritis, hearing loss, prior right hip fracture with ORIF
No known CKD; last outpatient labs reviewed.
HOME MEDS:
Amlodipine 5 mg PO daily
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
Aspirin 81 mg PO daily
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q8h PRN
Vitamin D 1000 units PO daily
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash
SOCIAL: lives alone in one-story home, daughter visits daily, walks with cane, no tobacco, no alcohol.
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Gen: elderly, ill-appearing, flushed, warm to touch.
Neuro: arouses to voice, oriented to self only, follows simple commands, no focal deficit, no neck rigidity.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no scleral icterus.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no JVD.
Pulm: tachypneic, shallow, clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheeze.
Abd: soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, no guarding, no CVA tenderness.
GU: no catheter, no vaginal discharge noted.
Ext: warm, no edema, cap refill 3 sec, no cellulitis, no sacral breakdown.
Skin: no rash, no petechiae.
ED COURSE:
2 large-bore IVs placed at 02:15.
[culture] Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
[antibiotic] Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added.
[bolus] Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Norepinephrine started peripherally at 03:20 for persistent hypotension, low dose.
LABS:
[creatinine] Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Na 132, K 4.6, Cl 99, HCO3 18, BUN 44, glucose 188.
AST 38, ALT 30, T bili 1.4, albumin 2.9, INR 1.3.
Troponin 0.04, flat on repeat.
IMAGING:
Chest x-ray portable: low lung volumes, no consolidation, no effusion.
CT abd/pelvis without contrast deferred given renal function; renal US ordered - no hydronephrosis.
ASSESSMENT:
88F with septic shock, urinary source most likely, complicated by acute kidney injury, thrombocytopenia, and hypoxemic respiratory compromise.
PLAN:
Admit to ICU.
Continue broad-spectrum IV antibiotics, narrow when cultures return.
Additional normal saline boluses as needed for MAP goal >65; wean pressor as able.
Hold lisinopril and amlodipine.
Strict I/O, foley placed for accurate output, daily BMP and CBC.
Supplemental O2 titrate to SpO2 >92%.
Delirium precautions, frequent reorientation, avoid benzodiazepines.
Discussed with daughter at 04:05; full code at this time.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning, ICU
lines: ICU PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:20
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt more interactive overnight, now oriented to self and place, still intermittently confused at night.
No agitation requiring restraint. Daughter stayed until 23:00.
Urine output 480 mL over past 12 hours via foley, cloudy.
EVENTS:
Norepinephrine weaned off at 05:40. BP 104/58 off pressor.
Additional 500 mL normal saline given at 02:00 for soft pressures.
Oxygen weaned from 6L NC to 3L NC, SpO2 94%.
[culture] Blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics remain pending at this time; gram stain of blood shows gram-negative rods.
[antibiotic] Continues piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h; vancomycin added on admission, trough pending.
LABS:
WBC 17,800, Hgb 10.4, platelets 91,000.
[creatinine] Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000 - repeat values improved as above.
Cr this morning 2.2, BUN 40, K 4.1, HCO3 21.
EXAM:
Gen: less toxic appearing, awake in bed.
Neuro: follows commands, no focal deficit.
Pulm: clear, less tachypneic on 3L NC.
Abd: soft, suprapubic tenderness improved.
Ext: no edema, warm, well perfused.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Sepsis, urinary source - improving hemodynamically off vasopressor. Continue IV antibiotics, await culture speciation.
2. AKI - trending down with volume resuscitation. Continue avoiding nephrotoxins, hold ACE inhibitor, renally dose meds, repeat BMP tonight.
3. Thrombocytopenia - likely sepsis related, follow daily, no bleeding.
4. Hypoxemia - wean O2 as tolerated, incentive spirometry, up to chair with PT.
5. Delirium - reorient, glasses and hearing aid at bedside, mobilize during day, no sedatives.
6. Dispo - likely transfer to floor later today if remains off pressor.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD5, Medical Floor
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD5, 08:05
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports feeling much better, ate most of breakfast, ambulated to bathroom with walker and one assist.
Back to baseline per daughter - conversant, oriented to self, place, time, and situation.
No fever reported by RN overnight. Tmax 37.1 C.
Foley removed HD4, voiding spontaneously, no dysuria today.
MICRO:
[culture] Blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours; urine culture with same organism, pan-sensitive.
[antibiotic] Remained on IV antibiotics through day 3; vancomycin discontinued HD3 after cultures; transitioned to targeted oral therapy HD4.
LABS:
WBC 8,900, no bands reported. Platelets 168,000.
Cr 1.1 this morning, BUN 18, K 4.0, HCO3 24.
[creatinine] Baseline comparison noted: Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000 at presentation, both now near baseline.
EXAM:
Gen: elderly female sitting up in chair, comfortable.
Neuro: alert, oriented x4, no deficit.
Pulm: clear bilaterally, on room air with SpO2 95%.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, BP 128/70.
Abd: soft, nontender, no suprapubic tenderness.
Ext: trace ankle edema, no calf tenderness.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. E. coli bacteremia with urinary source, sepsis resolved - afebrile, WBC normalized. Complete oral course, total 10 days therapy planned.
2. AKI resolved - restart lisinopril at discharge with outpatient BMP in 1 week.
3. Thrombocytopenia resolved.
4. Delirium resolved, back to baseline cognition.
5. Deconditioning - PT worked with pt yesterday, recommends home PT and walker.
6. Dispo - anticipate discharge home with daughter tomorrow if continues to tolerate oral intake and ambulation.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Sepsis, E. coli Bacteremia, Urinary Source
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission: HD1. Discharge: HD6. Total length of stay 6 days.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Septic shock secondary to urinary tract infection with E. coli bacteremia
2. Acute kidney injury, resolved
3. Sepsis-associated thrombocytopenia, resolved
4. Acute hypoxemic respiratory insufficiency, resolved
5. Hyperactive-hypoactive delirium, resolved
6. Hypertension, type 2 diabetes, chronic diastolic heart failure
HOSPITAL COURSE:
88-year-old female presented at 02:10 with fever and confusion.
[GCS] Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
[WBC] Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
[respiratory rate] Respiratory rate 30; SpO2 88% on RA, placed on 6L NC with SpO2 93%.
[culture] Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
[bolus] Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
[antibiotic] Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
Brief peripheral norepinephrine requirement, weaned off HD2 at 05:40 after further normal saline.
[creatinine] Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
[culture] Blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours, pan-sensitive; vancomycin stopped HD3.
Transitioned to oral targeted therapy HD4. Foley removed HD4. Renal function returned to 1.0 mg/dL and platelets to 182,000 by discharge.
Oxygen weaned to room air HD3. Cognition returned to baseline by HD4 per daughter.
PT evaluated and recommended walker plus home therapy.
CONDITION AT DISCHARGE: stable, afebrile, ambulating with walker, tolerating diet, BP 126/68 seated.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Oral antibiotic per sensitivities to complete 10-day total course, 4 days remaining
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily - resumed at discharge
Amlodipine 5 mg PO daily - resumed
Aspirin 81 mg PO daily
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q8h PRN pain
Vitamin D 1000 units PO daily
FOLLOW-UP:
Primary care in 5-7 days with BMP and CBC.
Home health nursing and home PT arranged, first visit within 48 hours.
Return precautions reviewed with pt and daughter: fever, confusion, decreased urine output, dizziness, poor oral intake.
Daughter verbalized understanding of medication list and follow-up plan.
